_note: Emergency decision tree for the 'crewmate collapsed' scenario. Each step is labelled 'Published' (wording checked against an opened publication, cited in source) or 'Demo copy' (team wording, not a protocol). tests/emergency.test.ts checks every link, label and source. No medication or dosing advice anywhere.
limitsNote: Hinkelbein et al. 2020 covers weightlessness only. CPR has never been performed on a human in spaceflight.

steps.text: Is the crewmember conscious and responsive to voice?
steps.hint: Say their name, tap the shoulder. Ten seconds, no longer.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Mockup cites Hinkelbein et al. 2020 (not yet opened by the team).

steps.text: Are they breathing regularly, not just gasping?
steps.hint: Look, listen and feel for no more than ten seconds. Occasional gasps do not count as breathing.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Mockup cites Hinkelbein et al. 2020 (not yet opened by the team).

steps.text: Restrain them, keep the airway open, attach the monitor and stay with them
steps.hint: Call the crew medical officer now. If breathing stops, go back one step and answer NO.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Not from a published protocol.

steps.text: Start chest compressions now and call for the defibrillator
steps.hint: Use the Evetts-Russomano method first. If you cannot compress well with it, switch to the Reverse-Bear-Hug method. Once they are restrained on the crew medical restraint system, use the Handstand method if the spacecraft's size allows it. Rate, depth and breaths are the same as in your Earth-based CPR training. Use the defibrillator only once they are restrained on an electrically isolated surface.
steps.label: Published
steps.source: Hinkelbein et al. 2020, Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med (https://doi.org/10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y), Recommendations 2, 3 and 10. The guideline gives no compression rate, depth or ratio of its own and refers to the Earth-based AHA/ERC guidelines, so no numbers are shown.

steps.text: Is the pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back, or are they short of breath?
steps.hint: Ask them to point to where it hurts. Watch the breathing while they answer.
steps.logYes: Spreading pain or short of breath
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. The CPR guideline does not cover a conscious crewmember with chest pain.

steps.text: Keep them at rest and restrained, attach the monitor and call the crew medical officer now
steps.hint: Do not give any medication from this screen. If they stop responding, restart from step 1.
steps.logYes: At rest, monitor on, medical officer called
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Not from a published protocol.

steps.text: Keep them at rest, attach the monitor and recheck every five minutes
steps.hint: If the pain spreads, breathing changes or they stop responding, restart from step 1.
steps.label: Demo copy
steps.source: Team draft. Not from a published protocol.
